name: Clams Casino
notes: The atmospheric foundation of this lane, and the most restrained model on it. Four parameters carry the research. (1) "The pitch centre is whatever the source sample lands on after time-stretching" — so `session.keys` is opened back up to all twelve minor centres against the genre's five, which is the single most distinctive thing in this file. (2) "Basic drum tracks" is the documented descriptor and the research says to take it literally: kick on 1 with one pickup, clap on 3, 8th hats, **no rolls, no percussion layers**. So `kick.densityPerBar` is 2–3 at `syncopation` 0.15, `percs.lanes` is empty, and the drums sit *behind* the wash — `velocityTiers` are the quietest in this batch, topping out at 104 with mains at 66–80, which is how "softened transients" reads in MIDI. (3) Harmony is tonic-by-drone with unresolved suspensions; where movement exists it is a two-chord oscillation, i–VI or i–iv, and nothing else. `maxChords` is 2, `susOrDimProb` is 0.42, and `chords.impliedByRiff` is set with `chordDurationBeats` running to 32 beats — the chord variety here is *how long the loop sits*, not what it plays, because adding families he does not play would be the dishonest fix for the 55-distinct-outputs floor. (4) The lead instrument is pitched, chopped, reversed vocal fragments in a high thin register over an empty mid-band: `melody.register` 76–100, 1–4 notes a bar, `timbreHint` `pitched_vocal_chop`. ⛔ The hat-roll block is the one place this file fights its own research. The batch fingerprint requires a `rolls` block at `freqPerBar` 0.45, but the paragraph says "no rolls" — so the vocab is weighted 6:1 to plain `16` and `velocityRamp` is off, which makes the "roll" a bare 16th inside an 8th-note hat line. That is the nearest honest thing; the 0.45 is the batch floor, not a reading of the record. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it high-medium and marks DAW/gear specifics and tempi `[LOW-CONF]` — the INFERRED parameters are the bpm range and the `velocityTiers` numbers. ⚠ The twelve keys carry an explicit twelve-long weights array, and that is not decoration: dark-trap authors five keys AND five weights, so overriding values alone left the merged model with five weights against twelve values — well-formed in this file and rejected once merged. Any model that widens a values list must restate its weights. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.6 to 0.61.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.6 over this model's 8-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 938 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 938/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,4] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 969/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 969/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide. ⚠ `melody.emptyBarBias` reduced again, 0.1 → 0.04, after the countermelody was still short of the 980 floor. An empty bar yields an empty counter region and every empty region is identical, so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. ⚠ `melody.emptyBarBias` removed entirely (was 0.04). Even at 0.04 it held the countermelody just under the 980 floor: an empty bar gives the counter nothing to answer and every empty answer is identical, so a model this close to the line cannot afford any. The lead keeps its space through density and phrasing instead, which vary per seed — silence does not. ⚠ **`countermelody.styles` weight on `sustain_pad` cut from 3 to 1**, which is what was actually saturating the counter (this model reached 963/1000 against a floor of 980). A probe over 1000 seeds showed the collisions were almost all ONE-NOTE counters: a single note at tick 240 held for the whole clip. That is the pad over a one-chord vamp — `maxChords` 2, `harmonicRhythm` weighted to `vamp`, `chordDurationBeats` running to the length of the clip — and `pad_notes` writes one note per chord event, so the only things a seed can vary are its pitch and whether it breathes. About a fifth of all seeds landed in that space and collided with each other. The pad is a **bed**, which is what this file already called it, not the counter’s usual answer; at weight 1 it is still there and the answering styles carry the rest. ⛔ The deeper gap is in the engine and is logged as `TASK-165`: a pad held as a single note across eight bars is not what a pad does, and every drone model in volumes 2–5 will meet this.
